# wg

> One local binary for sgrep-compatible semantic code search and exact
> ripgrep-compatible text search, with one shared daemon for semantic search
> and text-index pruning.

## Install

Download the archive from GitHub Releases. Unpack it, enter the extracted
directory, and add `bin/` to PATH. The archive contains `bin/wg` or `bin/wg.exe`.

From a checkout: `cargo install --locked --path . --bin wg`.

From the repository: `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/holdfast-labs/wgrep wgrep --bin wg`.

Requirements: Rust 1.95+ and a C linker/build tools (`cc` on Linux and macOS,
MSVC build tools on Windows) to build from source. Linux x64, Windows x64,
macOS arm64, or macOS x64. The macOS x64 archive is built by cross-compilation
and smoke-tested under Rosetta 2. macOS has no benchmark numbers (all
benchmarks are Linux), and the macOS cache is `~/.cache/wgrep`. The first
semantic run downloads about 58 MB of model and parser assets. No `rg` binary
is needed. Release archives ship only the `wg` binary.

## Docs

- README: README.md
- Agent guide: docs/agent-guide.md
- Benchmarks: docs/benchmarks.md

## Commands

- wg up [PATH] [--model auto|code|text] [--json]
- wg QUERY [ROOT] [--top N|-k N] [--json] [--explain] [--model auto|code|text]
- wg [RIPGREP-FLAGS] PATTERN [PATH...]
- wg status [--json]
- wg down

## Contract

- Default route is sgrep-compatible semantic ranking. The parity reference is
  pinned sgrep revision `0fbe8e5`. Results are ranked, not exhaustive.
  `--top N` / `-k N` sets the count (1..=100, default 5).
- A ripgrep flag (`-F`, `-e`, `-n`, `-l`, `-g`, `--files`, and others) selects
  the in-process ripgrep 15.1 engine. Output, exit status, ignore rules, and
  encodings follow `rg` 15.1.0. No `rg` binary is needed.
- The daemon keeps one live semantic index and one trigram text index per
  attached root. One watcher per root feeds both indexes. One model pool is
  shared between roots.
- The text route runs in the `wg` process. It uses the trigram index only for a
  default directory walk under an attached root. Flags that change the file set
  (`-g`, `--hidden`, `--json`, an explicit file) use a full scan. A fallback
  changes speed, not results.
- Always give text-route commands an explicit path. With no path, `rg` reads
  stdin when stdin is a pipe. Use `-` to read stdin on purpose.
- `--json` alone is a semantic JSON array. `--json` with ripgrep flags is
  ripgrep JSON events.
- Semantic scope is one whole attached root. A file or subdirectory semantic
  scope returns an explicit error.
- `wg status --json` reports readiness. A ready root has `ready: true`,
  `pending: 0`, and `text` not null or `text_error` a string.
- `wg up` is safe under captured output. The daemon is detached and inherits
  only its log.
- `wg up --json` always includes `pid`, the daemon PID. This holds for a new
  build, a joined build, and an already attached root.
- `wg up` checks the path before it starts the daemon. A missing path or a file
  fails with `not a directory`.
- `wg down` is idempotent. With no daemon it exits 0 and prints
  `No wg service is running.` The JSON reply is `{"ok":true,"running":false}`.
- `wg status` with no daemon exits 2 and prints
  `wg: no wg service is running for this cache; run wg up first`.
- The model is fixed at `wg up`. A mismatch error names the attached model and
  says: run `wg down`, then `wg up --model <m>`.
- On Windows, human-readable output removes the `\\?\` prefix from paths. JSON
  keeps the canonical path.
- A failed build is retried by the next single `wg up`.
- Exit codes: 0 matches or success, 1 no matches, 2 error.
